title: Executable Constraint Surface packet
description: A machine-checkable specification packet for one kernel. THE PACKET IS THE INDEPENDENT VARIABLE of this experiment: completeness is manipulated across arms, so what a packet may contain is itself preregistered. Per PREREG §8 and SPEC §9 the rendered packet is one of exactly three permitted prompt inputs, alongside the C signature and (repair only) the current gate's feedback. Anything a packet can express, a generator can see. Anything it cannot express is either pinned by another channel or left unpinned — see evidence/choice_point_map.md.

kernel.description: Must match a kernel in SPEC §5 and a row in kernel_signatures.json. The frozen v1 set is closed; adding a kernel is a v1.1 supersession.

prereg_tag.description: Packets are valid only against the frozen preregistration.

completeness.description: Which arm this packet belongs to. 'weak' is the dose-response variant of SPEC §11 arm 3: forbidden list dropped, budgets dropped, half the vectors withheld. Prediction on record: D and variance RISE under 'weak'.

signature.description: The exact C prototype. MUST match SPEC §5 and both sealed oracle prototypes — enforced by harness/gates/prearm_check.py, which compares type sequences rather than strings.

domain.description: Input constraints. A packet MUST NOT claim to constrain behaviour outside the domain it declares; the vector gate refuses out-of-domain vectors for exactly this reason.

element_range.description: Inclusive [lo, hi] bound on element values where the kernel declares one.

pointer_precondition.description: Decided option 2, board #13818: pointers valid and non-null for n>0. Behaviour for NULL with n>0 is OUT OF DOMAIN — undefined, untested, and never a vector.

semantics.description: Prose statement of required behaviour. This is the channel whose completeness the experiment manipulates. Where it is silent, the choice-point map records what pins the bit instead — or that nothing does.

check_values.description: Published external anchors, where the kernel has any. crc32 has one; most kernels do not. An anchor is stronger evidence than an oracle pair because it is independent of both seats.

forbidden.description: Constructs gate 1 rejects. EMPTY IS LEGAL AND MEANINGFUL: the 'weak' arm drops this list, and an empty array is how that is expressed rather than by omitting the key. Omission would be indistinguishable from an authoring mistake.

budgets.description: Gate 6 caps. Sanity bounds, not optimisation targets (SPEC §7). Empty object is legal and is how the 'weak' arm drops budgets. NOTE per LN-3: budget rejection is BIDIRECTIONAL on D — it inflates when it removes a largest-cluster member and deflates when it removes a minority one, so the budget-only rejection count is co-reported with its direction marked unresolved.

implementation_hint.description: OPTIONAL and DELIBERATELY SEGREGATED. A hint steers implementation without constraining behaviour, so it acts on the implementation-text variance endpoint while leaving D untouched — see choice_point_map.md §4. Of the v1 set only median3x3_u8 carries one ('sorting-network friendly'). Kept as its own key rather than folded into `semantics` so that hint-bearing cells are mechanically identifiable at analysis time and cannot be silently counted as specification content.

notes.description: Non-normative. Never rendered into a prompt.
